clue.text: Sketch of carriage shaft

parts.note: port is an old word for carriage or bearing, how one holds oneself
a shaft of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A drawing of the pole on a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle, but here it is deportment; 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them, as an artist does in a quick drawing.

clue.text: When at work he'll face the wall

definitions.text: When at work he'll face the wall

parts.words: When at work he'll face the wall
parts.note: not someone facing a firing squad but a tradesman who spreads a smooth coat over walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'face the wall' sounds like facing execution, but it means covering a wall with a smooth surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman applies a smooth coating to interior walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Establishing a radical system

definitions.meaning: setting firmly in place, as roots do
radical here means of roots, so a network of roots

explanation.definitionFit: Rooting means fixing something firmly, and a plant's rooting is its root network, radical meaning relating to roots.

clue.text: The governor got a ruler replaced

indicators.note: replaced signals that the letters of got a ruler are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: The head of state got a new monarch installed.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor on an engine is a device controlling speed, a mechanical controller.

clue.text: Measure the area

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of three feet
an enclosed piece of ground beside a building

explanation.definitionFit: A yard is three feet of length, and also an enclosed space behind or around a building.

clue.text: Hacks writing about fish

indicators.note: about means the writing letters go around the fish word

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Journalists writing up a piece about fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' looks like journalists, but it is a verb: mutilates or chops roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle is to cut or tear something roughly, just as one hacks at it.

clue.text: One can't interrupt repairs for the poor beggars!

indicators.note: interrupt means the one-can't letters break into the middle of the repairs word

parts.note: mends means repairs
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A charity cannot stop helping the destitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicants are people who live by begging, such as friars of mendicant orders.

clue.text: Having a smell with nitrogen is risky

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
iffy means dubious or risky

explanation.surface: A smelly gas mixture is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: NIFFY is British slang for smelly; 'with' and 'is' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal: something niffy gives off a nasty odour.

clue.text: .24 ac allowed nine to change inside

indicators.note: inside means the reworked number goes within the allowed word

parts.note: lent means allowed, as in lent itself to

indicators.note: to change signals that the letters of nine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Permission given for nine to get changed indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 24 across. 'to change' jumbles the number into NIEN, which 'inside' places within the allowed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient and humane both describe someone merciful and forgiving.

clue.text: Soundly tie up a piece of meat

indicators.note: Soundly tells us the word spoken is the one heard, not the one spelt

parts.note: to stake a plant is to tie it up to a post

explanation.surface: Firmly truss a joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'securely' but tells us the tie-up word is heard, giving a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice of beef or other meat.

clue.text: A pine from end to end

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A pine tree measured right through its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Going along a road means travelling its length, end to end.

clue.text: It gives all-round protection to a receiver of jewelry

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewelry
a fence is criminal slang for a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Something that guards a dealer in stolen gems on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is someone who buys and sells stolen property; 'to a' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring fence encloses an area completely, so it guards it on every side.

clue.text: Just a little sweet

definitions.meaning: a layered dessert of sponge, custard, fruit and cream

explanation.definitionFit: A trifle means a small amount, and is also a British cold pudding of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.

clue.text: A local newsagent in America

parts.note: not a shop selling papers but the department of a US newspaper that gathers local news

explanation.walkthrough: 'Newsagent' suggests a British corner shop selling papers; read it as an agent of news, a newsroom section.
explanation.definitionFit: In American journalism this is the editorial section covering news of the home town.

clue.text: Sort of fight nobody will pay to see

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
a show that costs nothing and is open to anyone

explanation.definitionFit: A brawl where anyone joins in is so called, and the phrase read literally means admission costs nothing to anybody.

clue.text: Correct title

definitions.meaning: a legal entitlement, as in a title to land

explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is right, and a right is also a legal claim or entitlement to property.

clue.text: The odd article is true-to life

indicators.note: odd signals that the letters of the words article is are set in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A strange piece in the paper turns out to be lifelike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ARTICLE IS; 'The' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic picture represents things as they actually are, lifelike.

clue.text: Irresponsible and ill-mannered outside right

indicators.note: outside means the ill-mannered word stands around the letter for right

parts.note: impudent means cheeky or ill-mannered

explanation.surface: A rude, reckless person stands outside on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise and careless of consequences.

clue.text: Called round on only one occasion, though far from modest

indicators.note: round means the called word goes around the occasion word

parts.note: cited means summoned or called, as before a court
once means a single time

explanation.surface: Visited just the once, yet very vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called round' suggests visiting; split it so 'round' is the container signal. 'though' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain and having too high an opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Soldiers and general coming back again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
current means prevailing or generally accepted, as in current opinion

explanation.surface: Troops and their commander return once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' wants to be an army officer; here it is an adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurrent happens repeatedly, returning time after time.

clue.text: This act had to be ordered with care perhaps

indicators.note: to be ordered signals that the letters of had and care are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The performance needed to be put together carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words; 'perhaps' marks the definition as one kind of act.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a pretence or absurd performance, an act put on for show.

clue.text: Flat in need of decoration?

definitions.meaning: unadorned, simple, which might call for ornament

explanation.definitionFit: A plain is level open country, and plain also means unornamented and simple.

clue.text: Greed is a failing holding the painter up

indicators.note: holding means the failing word grips the turned painter letters inside

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the painter letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Avarice is a weakness that keeps the artist from rising.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns the painter's letters to read AR, and 'holding' sets them within the failing word; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme desire for wealth, a grasping covetousness.

clue.text: Company account — it turned on compulsion

indicators.note: turned means the little word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A firm's books show it switched on under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses only IT to make TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaction is a rare word for force or constraint applied to someone.

clue.text: This chain is about strong enough

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
able means capable, strong enough

explanation.surface: A chain that is roughly sturdy enough for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links; a cable is also the heavy chain or rope of a ship's anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's anchor cable is a heavy rope or chain, and cable is also a nautical measure.

clue.text: Saw "x" taking over

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
on can mean over or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a cross while taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense of see; it is the noun, the tool. 'taking' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting joints, so the word names that kind of saw.

clue.text: 7 dn put a guy in the shade

indicators.note: in means the guy is set inside the colour word

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a man is a guy, a fellow

explanation.surface: Treat a fellow kindly by sitting him in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 7 down, LENIENT; 'put' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane and lenient are synonyms: both mean showing mercy and compassion.

clue.text: The bank seems to be in a knot

definitions.meaning: a ridge of rock or sand just under the sea

definitions.text: seems to be in a knot
definitions.meaning: a square knot used by sailors, called after this word

explanation.definitionFit: A reef is an underwater ridge or bank, and the sailor's reef knot carries the same name.

clue.text: Showing fortitude about a surprising win is an inspiration

indicators.note: about means the brave word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: brave means showing courage or fortitude

indicators.note: surprising signals that the letters of win are jumbled into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A courageous player's shock victory was a stroke of genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' rearranges WIN to INW, which with A sits within the courage word under 'about'; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever idea, a flash of inspiration.

clue.text: In the dictionary the meaning's given as "Order"

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the words the dictionary, spanning both

explanation.surface: A dictionary definition that simply says order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the meaning's given as' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command.

clue.text: Oriental flier, a trainee, going on and on

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern, oriental
a tern is a seabird, a flier
L is for learner, the plate a trainee driver displays in Britain

explanation.surface: An Eastern bird and a novice keep on going.
explanation.walkthrough: The L comes from the L-plate shown by learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever without end.

clue.text: Stout leader, but a fool

parts.note: stout means fat, plump
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: A portly boss who is nevertheless an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' might suggest the dark beer; here it means plump. 'but' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, a dolt.
